page: Vultr voc-m-1c-8gb-50s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring a dedicated AMD EPYC processor with 1 vCPU, 1 physical core, and 1 thread per core, clocked at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, and 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and lacks GPU acceleration.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core capabilities, with the stress-ng single-core CPU test scoring 2896.39 and the Geekbench single-core test scoring 1999.0, both placing in the top 25% of tested servers. However, due to the single-core constraint, multi-core performance is limited, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 1961.0 and stress-ng multi-core scoring 2896.39, both falling into lower performance tiers. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth at 22.42 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 20.94 GB/sec.

This server offers a specialized resource profile, pairing a dedicated CPU core with a relatively high memory allocation. This makes it a cost-efficient option for workloads that require dedicated, non-shared CPU execution but do not benefit from multi-threaded parallelization. It is well-suited for single-threaded applications, lightweight text processing, small-scale caching, and basic background workers that require a stable memory footprint without high multi-core compute demands.

It is best suited for single-threaded applications, text processing, and lightweight caching.
